justification: All four round-1 quote problems are genuinely fixed, verified by fetching the live pages myself rather than trusting the diff. (1) nvie.com: the article now attributes 'allow[s] for minor bug fixes and preparing meta-data for a release' and 'adding large new features here is strictly prohibited' to the release-branch paragraph -- live fetch returns 'they allow for minor bug fixes and preparing meta-data for a release (version number, build dates, etc.)' and 'Adding large new features here is strictly prohibited. They must be merged into develop...' Both fragments match; the fabricated 'new small bugfixes ... other than that, no new features' sentence is gone. (2) trunkbaseddevelopment.com release-branch quote now reads '...release branches that are cut from the trunk on a just-in-time basis, are "hardened" before a release ... and those branches are deleted some time after release' -- live fetch returns the identical sentence verbatim ('cut from the trunk', not 'are created'). (3) The feature-flags quote now reads teams '"use feature flags in day to day development to allow for hedging on the order of releases"' -- live fetch confirms 'use', matching exactly. (4) Conventional Commits now reads a breaking change bumps MAJOR '"regardless of type"' -- two independent live fetches of the spec both return 'regardless of type, should be translated to MAJOR releases', an exact match. Nothing was fabricated or altered in any of the four repaired passages. I also re-checked eight quotes round 1 had already verified and none had regressed: the master/develop HEAD definitions, the hotfix-branches sentence, the --no-ff defense, the full 2020 note (multiple-versions / web-apps / 'shoehorn git-flow' sentences), the six-step GitHub Flow list plus its three supporting sentences, and the trunk-based-development one-line definition -- all still match the live pages. Two small new items, both nits rather than fabrications, worth the writer's attention but not score-capping: (a) the trunk-based-development opening quote inserts an ellipsis between "'trunk'" and "and resist" that implies text was cut there; the live source runs those two phrases together with no gap ('...called 'trunk' and resist any pressure...'), the only material elision is the trailing 'by employing documented techniques', which the article drops silently at the end instead -- the words quoted are all accurate, only the ellipsis is misplaced, so this is a precision nit, not a fabrication; (b) the tag paragraph in the trunk-based section ('-a makes this an annotated tag, a real object with its own message and date rather than a bare pointer') restates a fact how-git-works.md already covers in its own dedicated section ('The fourth object type: the annotated tag': 'An annotated tag is a real object... points at the commit and carries its own author, date and message') and cites git-scm.com/docs/git-tag instead of linking to that sibling section; it is one clause, not a re-derivation with worked examples, but the cleaner move is a cross-link. Everything round 1 already found strong is unchanged, because the fix touched only the four flagged sentences: originality remains genuinely high (three independently executed branch histories with real teammate scenarios and measured git rev-list numbers, not the diagram-and-prose genre the comparable Atlassian page uses), no filler, no keyword stuffing, no ad code, all 9 front-matter sources are cited inline with no orphans, and the article still explicitly defers merge mechanics to branching-and-merging.md and object/ref internals to how-git-works.md rather than re-deriving them (aside from the one small annotated-tag overlap noted above). `node tools/run-code.mjs src/content/articles/version-control/git-workflows.md` passes: 'PASS version-control/git-workflows.md blocks=36 executed=18'. I did not run tools/verify-page.mjs (screenshots, Lighthouse, console/link check); that is the design critic's assignment, so consoleErrors and brokenLinks are left null rather than guessed and play no part in this score.

issues.location: ## Trunk-based development section, opening paragraph: "developers collaborate on code in a single branch called 'trunk' ... and resist any pressure to create other long-lived development branches."
issues.problem: The ellipsis sits between "'trunk'" and "and resist", but the live source runs those two phrases together with nothing omitted there ('...single branch called 'trunk' and resist any pressure to create other long-lived development branches by employing documented techniques.'). The words quoted are accurate, but the ellipsis marks an omission that is not where the real elision is -- the sentence actually drops its trailing clause ('by employing documented techniques') silently at the end, with no ellipsis there at all.
issues.fixLooksLike: Move or remove the ellipsis: either quote the sentence straight through to 'long-lived development branches' with no mid-quote ellipsis (since nothing is cut there), or, if the trailing clause should be flagged as dropped, end the quote with '...branches ...' before the closing quotation mark.
